highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most powerful model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should be aware of this new model as it may become available as a selectable option within their coding sessions, potentially offering improved reasoning and code generation capabilities.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Anthropic has made 'Auto mode' the default setting in Claude Code, meaning the tool will now automatically select the best model and approach for your task without requiring manual configuration. This is a great quality-of-life improvement for beginners who previously had to understand model differences before getting started.

highlights.title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports cross-session messaging, allowing different Claude Code instances to communicate with each other. This is a powerful feature for advanced workflows where you might run parallel agents on different parts of a project and need them to coordinate or share context.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.229 Released
highlights.summary: The latest Claude Code release adds support for resuming Remote Control sessions via `claude remote-control --continue`, server-supplied hook support for self-hosted runners, and SSE keepalive pings for more stable gateway streaming. If you use Claude Code in CI/CD pipelines or with self-hosted runners, the new hook support brings parity with managed environments.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.228 Released — Bug Fixes for Windows and TUI
highlights.summary: This release fixes a critical bug where interactive sessions could stop redrawing while the process kept running, which could leave users confused about whether Claude Code was still working. Windows users also benefit from a fix ensuring Git and Git Bash are correctly detected even when Claude Code is launched from a parent folder of the Git installation.

highlights.title: Claude Code is Leaking Real Email Addresses as a User-Agent String in curl Commands
highlights.summary: A security issue has been reported where Claude Code inadvertently includes the user's real email address in the User-Agent string of curl commands it generates, potentially exposing personal information in logs or to third-party servers. Developers should be aware of this issue and avoid sharing curl command outputs publicly until a fix is confirmed.

highlights.title: Learn 80% of Claude Code in 10 Minutes (2026 Tutorial)
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial promises to cover the most important 80% of Claude Code's features in just 10 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a quick but comprehensive overview. It's a great starting point if you're new to Claude Code and want to get productive fast without sitting through a lengthy course.

highlights.title: Token Monitor — An ESP32-S3 Desktop Display for Tracking AI Coding Assistant Usage
highlights.summary: A community member built a physical desktop display using an ESP32-S3 microcontroller that shows real-time token usage from AI coding assistants like Claude Code. This fun hardware project is useful for developers on usage-based plans who want a constant visual reminder of their consumption without checking dashboards.

tips_of_the_day: If you're on a usage-based or Max plan, run `claude remote-control --continue` after a disconnect to resume your most recent session without losing context — no need to re-explain your task from scratch.
Before sharing any curl commands generated by Claude Code in public forums or bug reports, inspect the User-Agent header for personal information such as your email address, and redact it if present.

Take advantage of the new Auto mode default: instead of manually selecting a model, let Claude Code pick the right one for each task — this works especially well when switching between quick edits and complex multi-file refactors in the same session.
